# Collider Wireframe Debug View Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** F3 toggles a wireframe view of every physics collider (voxel chunk colliders + entity capsules) near the player, generated by rapier's own `DebugRenderPipeline` on the game thread and drawn as Bevy gizmos.

**Architecture:** The vendored rapier fork already ships `DebugRenderPipeline` behind the `debug-render` feature. A `DebugRenderBackend` collector in the `game` crate turns collider outlines into plain `DebugLine` buffers per region (region-local coords, radius-filtered around the viewer); the client's `GameInstanceManager` emits them per tick over the existing `ClientUpdateEvent` channel; a Bevy system shifts each buffer by its region's `world_offset()` and draws with `Gizmos`. An `Arc<AtomicBool>` inside `game::DebugFlags` (not sim state — never in rollback, `GameData`, or the wire protocol) carries the F3 toggle from the render thread to the game thread.

**Tech Stack:** Rust, vendored rapier3d fork (`debug-render` feature), Bevy 0.18 (`bevy_gizmos`), crossbeam channels.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-collider-debug-render-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- `game` and `server` crates stay Bevy-free and windowing-free; the collector lives in `game` and uses only rapier/std types.
- `DebugFlags`, `DebugLine`, and `ClientUpdateEvent::DebugLines` must never enter `GameData`, the rollback log, or the wire protocol (`ClientPacket`/`ServerPacket` bincode) — they are process-local render plumbing. No simulation math changes, so determinism is untouched.
- Never disable rollback hash verification.
- Vendored forks (`crates/rapier` etc.): feature-flag flips only, no source edits.
- `Real = OrderedFloat<f32>` in this workspace — unwrap to `f32` with `.0` (same as `convert.rs`); wrap with `Real::from(x)`.
- Rapier's `DebugColor = [f32; 4]` is **HSLA**, not RGBA — convert with `Color::hsla` on the Bevy side.
- Tunables are named constants (`DEBUG_COLLIDER_RADIUS`), even without a UI.
- Tag any test measured >100ms with `#[ignore = "slow: >100ms — run via just test-full"]`.
- The `justfile` is canonical for commands; this feature adds no new commands, so it should not change.
- Commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

```rust
//! Collider wireframe debug view: an engine-neutral `DebugRenderBackend`
//! that collects rapier's debug-render line callbacks into plain buffers,
//! radius-filtered around the viewer. Consumed by the client, which ships
//! the buffers to the render thread per region. Not sim state — nothing
//! here may touch GameData, the rollback log, or the wire protocol. See
//! docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-collider-debug-render-design.md.

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use rapier3d::math::{Real, Vector};
    use rapier3d::prelude::{ColliderBuilder, ColliderSet, RigidBodyBuilder, RigidBodySet};

    /// A fixed body with a 2×2×2 cuboid at the origin, viewer at the origin.
    fn one_cuboid() -> (RigidBodySet, ColliderSet) {
        let mut bodies = RigidBodySet::new();
        let mut colliders = ColliderSet::new();
        let body = bodies.insert(RigidBodyBuilder::fixed().build());
        colliders.insert_with_parent(
            ColliderBuilder::cuboid(Real::from(1.0), Real::from(1.0), Real::from(1.0)).build(),
            body,
            &mut bodies,
        );
        (bodies, colliders)
    }

    #[test]
    fn cuboid_emits_wireframe_lines_near_viewer() {
        let (bodies, colliders) = one_cuboid();
        let mut dbg = ColliderDebug::default();
        let lines = dbg.collect(&bodies, &colliders, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]);
        // A cuboid outline is 12 edges; don't pin the exact count (style
        // subdivisions could change), just that it's a real wireframe whose
        // endpoints all sit on the unit cuboid's surface envelope.
        assert!(lines.len() >= 12, "expected a wireframe, got {} lines", lines.len());
        for l in &lines {
            for p in [l.a, l.b] {
                assert!(
                    p.iter().all(|c| c.abs() <= 1.0 + 1e-3),
                    "endpoint {:?} escapes the 2x2x2 cuboid",
                    p
                );
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn radius_filter_excludes_far_colliders() {
        let (mut bodies, mut colliders) = one_cuboid();
        let near_only = {
            let mut dbg = ColliderDebug::default();
            dbg.collect(&bodies, &colliders, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]).len()
        };
        // Add a second cuboid far beyond DEBUG_COLLIDER_RADIUS.
        let far = bodies.insert(
            RigidBodyBuilder::fixed()
                .translation(Vector::new(
                    Real::from(1000.0),
                    Real::from(0.0),
                    Real::from(0.0),
                ))
                .build(),
        );
        colliders.insert_with_parent(
            ColliderBuilder::cuboid(Real::from(1.0), Real::from(1.0), Real::from(1.0)).build(),
            far,
            &mut bodies,
        );
        let mut dbg = ColliderDebug::default();
        let lines = dbg.collect(&bodies, &colliders, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]);
        assert_eq!(lines.len(), near_only, "far collider must be filtered out");
        // Viewer standing next to the far collider sees it (and not the near one).
        let lines_far = dbg.collect(&bodies, &colliders, [1000.0, 0.0, 0.0]);
        assert_eq!(lines_far.len(), near_only, "same shape, same line count");
        assert!(lines_far.iter().all(|l| l.a[0] > 500.0 && l.b[0] > 500.0));
    }

    #[test]
    fn dynamic_bodies_render_with_distinct_color() {
        let (mut bodies, mut colliders) = one_cuboid();
        let fixed_only = {
            let mut dbg = ColliderDebug::default();
            dbg.collect(&bodies, &colliders, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]).len()
        };
        // A dynamic ball next to the fixed cuboid (player capsule stand-in).
        let ball = bodies.insert(RigidBodyBuilder::dynamic().build());
        colliders.insert_with_parent(
            ColliderBuilder::ball(Real::from(0.5)).build(),
            ball,
            &mut bodies,
        );
        let mut dbg = ColliderDebug::default();
        let lines = dbg.collect(&bodies, &colliders, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]);
        assert!(lines.len() > fixed_only, "ball outline must add lines");
        // Fixed vs dynamic bodies get different HSLA colors from the style.
        let colors: std::collections::BTreeSet<[u32; 4]> =
            lines.iter().map(|l| l.color.map(f32::to_bits)).collect();
        assert!(colors.len() >= 2, "expected distinct fixed/dynamic colors");
    }

    #[test]
    fn flags_default_off_and_toggle() {
        let flags = DebugFlags::default();
        assert!(!flags.collider_wireframes());
        flags.set_collider_wireframes(true);
        assert!(flags.collider_wireframes());
        // Clones share the same underlying atomic.
        let clone = flags.clone();
        clone.set_collider_wireframes(false);
        assert!(!flags.collider_wireframes());
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Add the implementation above the tests in `debug_render.rs`**

```rust
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::sync::Arc;

use rapier3d::geometry::Aabb;
use rapier3d::math::{Point, Real};
use rapier3d::pipeline::{
    DebugColor, DebugRenderBackend, DebugRenderMode, DebugRenderObject, DebugRenderPipeline,
    DebugRenderStyle,
};
use rapier3d::prelude::{ColliderSet, RigidBodySet};

/// Only colliders whose AABB comes within this distance (world units) of the
/// viewer get debug wireframes. Keeps gizmo counts sane in dense
/// chisel-scale geometry; tune here.
pub const DEBUG_COLLIDER_RADIUS: f32 = 64.0;

/// One wireframe segment, region-local coordinates. `color` is HSLA exactly
/// as rapier's `DebugRenderStyle` emits it (fixed vs dynamic bodies get
/// different hues for free); the render side converts with `Color::hsla`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct DebugLine {
    pub a: [f32; 3],
    pub b: [f32; 3],
    pub color: [f32; 4],
}

/// Process-local debug toggles shared between the render thread (F3 handler)
/// and the game thread (line generation). Deliberately NOT sim state: never
/// serialized, never hashed, never in the rollback log. Clones share state.
#[derive(Clone, Default, Debug)]
pub struct DebugFlags {
    collider_wireframes: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl DebugFlags {
    pub fn set_collider_wireframes(&self, on: bool) {
        self.collider_wireframes.store(on, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
    pub fn collider_wireframes(&self) -> bool {
        self.collider_wireframes.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
}

/// Squared distance from a point to an AABB (0 inside).
fn aabb_dist_sq(aabb: &Aabb, p: &Point<Real>) -> Real {
    let mut d2 = Real::from(0.0);
    for i in 0..3 {
        let c = p[i].clamp(aabb.mins[i], aabb.maxs[i]);
        let d = c - p[i];
        d2 += d * d;
    }
    d2
}

/// `DebugRenderBackend` that buffers lines and drops colliders whose AABB is
/// beyond `DEBUG_COLLIDER_RADIUS` of the viewer.
struct LineCollector {
    lines: Vec<DebugLine>,
    viewer: Point<Real>,
    max_dist_sq: Real,
}

impl DebugRenderBackend for LineCollector {
    fn filter_object(&self, object: DebugRenderObject) -> bool {
        match object {
            DebugRenderObject::Collider(_, co) => {
                aabb_dist_sq(&co.compute_aabb(), &self.viewer) <= self.max_dist_sq
            }
            // Only COLLIDER_SHAPES mode runs, so nothing else is offered.
            _ => true,
        }
    }

    fn draw_line(
        &mut self,
        _object: DebugRenderObject,
        a: Point<Real>,
        b: Point<Real>,
        color: DebugColor,
    ) {
        // Real = OrderedFloat<f32>; .0 unwraps (same as convert.rs).
        self.lines.push(DebugLine {
            a: [a.x.0, a.y.0, a.z.0],
            b: [b.x.0, b.y.0, b.z.0],
            color,
        });
    }
}

/// Reusable wrapper around rapier's `DebugRenderPipeline` (the pipeline
/// caches unit outlines for curved shapes, so keep one alive per manager
/// instead of rebuilding per call).
pub struct ColliderDebug {
    pipeline: DebugRenderPipeline,
}

impl Default for ColliderDebug {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            pipeline: DebugRenderPipeline::new(
                DebugRenderStyle::default(),
                DebugRenderMode::COLLIDER_SHAPES,
            ),
        }
    }
}

impl ColliderDebug {
    /// Wireframe every collider within `DEBUG_COLLIDER_RADIUS` of `viewer`.
    /// All coordinates (input viewer, output lines) are region-local.
    pub fn collect(
        &mut self,
        bodies: &RigidBodySet,
        colliders: &ColliderSet,
        viewer: [f32; 3],
    ) -> Vec<DebugLine> {
        let mut backend = LineCollector {
            lines: Vec::new(),
            viewer: Point::new(
                Real::from(viewer[0]),
                Real::from(viewer[1]),
                Real::from(viewer[2]),
            ),
            max_dist_sq: Real::from(DEBUG_COLLIDER_RADIUS * DEBUG_COLLIDER_RADIUS),
        };
        self.pipeline
            .render_colliders(&mut backend, bodies, colliders);
        backend.lines
    }
}
```

Note for the implementer: if `p[i].clamp(...)` doesn't resolve on `Real` (Ord vs f32 clamp ambiguity), use `Ord::clamp(p[i], aabb.mins[i], aabb.maxs[i])` — `OrderedFloat<f32>` is `Ord`.

```rust
//! Headless proof of the collider-debug-line flow: flag on ⇒ per-region
//! DebugLines events with real content; flag off ⇒ silence (zero cost).
use client::harness::SimHarness;
use game::ClientUpdateEvent;

fn debug_line_events(evs: &[ClientUpdateEvent]) -> Vec<(game::RegionCoords, usize)> {
    evs.iter()
        .filter_map(|e| match e {
            ClientUpdateEvent::DebugLines(id, lines) => Some((*id, lines.len())),
            _ => None,
        })
        .collect()
}

#[test]
#[ignore = "slow: >100ms — run via just test-full"]
fn debug_lines_emit_when_enabled_and_stop_when_disabled() {
    let mut h = SimHarness::new();
    h.connect();
    h.drain_bridge_events(); // discard join-time noise

    // Off by default: ticks emit no DebugLines.
    h.step();
    assert!(
        debug_line_events(&h.drain_bridge_events()).is_empty(),
        "flag off must cost nothing"
    );

    // On: every loaded region gets a buffer each tick, and the home region's
    // is non-empty (terrain colliders sit under the spawned player).
    h.debug.set_collider_wireframes(true);
    let mut saw_nonempty = false;
    for _ in 0..5 {
        h.step();
        let evs = h.drain_bridge_events();
        let dbg = debug_line_events(&evs);
        if dbg.iter().any(|(_, n)| *n > 0) {
            saw_nonempty = true;
            break;
        }
    }
    assert!(saw_nonempty, "expected non-empty collider wireframes near the player");

    // Off again: silence resumes.
    h.debug.set_collider_wireframes(false);
    h.drain_bridge_events();
    h.step();
    assert!(debug_line_events(&h.drain_bridge_events()).is_empty());
}
```

```rust
    /// While the debug flag is on: wireframe every collider near the viewer,
    /// one buffer per loaded region, and ship them to the render bridge.
    /// Lines are region-local; the bridge adds each region's world offset.
    /// Runs after the tick (read-only), so it never touches the rollback log.
    fn emit_collider_debug_lines(&mut self) {
        if !self.debug_flags.collider_wireframes() {
            return;
        }
        // Viewer = local player's body, rebased to world space via home.
        let (Some(local), Some(home)) = (self.local_player_translation(), self.home_region)
        else {
            return; // no player body yet: no lines beats wrong lines
        };
        let hoff = home.world_offset();
        let world_pos = [local[0] + hoff[0], local[1] + hoff[1], local[2] + hoff[2]];
        let Some(world) = self.world.as_ref() else { return };
        for (id, region) in &world.regions {
            let off = id.world_offset();
            let viewer_local = [
                world_pos[0] - off[0],
                world_pos[1] - off[1],
                world_pos[2] - off[2],
            ];
            let data = region.data();
            let lines = self.collider_debug.collect(
                &*data.physics.bodies,
                &*data.physics.colliders,
                viewer_local,
            );
            let _ = self
                .client_event_send
                .send(ClientUpdateEvent::DebugLines(*id, lines));
        }
    }
```

(`&*data.physics.bodies` derefs the tier-2 `Undo<RigidBodySet>` wrapper to `&RigidBodySet` — reads through `Undo<T>: Deref` are the established pattern, see `viewer_region()` in this file.)

```rust
//! Collider wireframe debug view, render side: per-region line buffers
//! shipped from the game thread (`ClientUpdateEvent::DebugLines`), drawn as
//! world-space gizmos while the F3 overlay is visible. See
//! docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-08-collider-debug-render-design.md.
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use bevy::prelude::*;
use game::{DebugLine, RegionId};

use super::hud::DebugOverlay;

/// Latest collider wireframe buffer per region, region-local coordinates.
/// Written by `bridge::drain_client_updates` (replace-on-receipt); entries
/// drop on RemoveRegion; cleared wholesale when the overlay hides.
#[derive(Resource, Default)]
pub struct DebugColliderLines(pub BTreeMap<RegionId, Vec<DebugLine>>);

/// Render-side handle to the shared debug toggles. The same
/// `game::DebugFlags` lives in the game thread's manager; F3 flips it here.
#[derive(Resource, Clone)]
pub struct DebugFlagsRes(pub game::DebugFlags);

/// Draw the buffered wireframes while the F3 overlay is visible, shifting
/// each region's lines by its world offset (the sim is region-local; the
/// world offset exists only at this render boundary). When hidden, clear
/// the buffers once so stale geometry never flashes on the next toggle.
pub fn draw_collider_wireframes(
    overlay: Query<&Visibility, With<DebugOverlay>>,
    mut lines: ResMut<DebugColliderLines>,
    mut gizmos: Gizmos,
) {
    let visible = overlay.iter().any(|v| *v == Visibility::Visible);
    if !visible {
        if !lines.0.is_empty() {
            lines.0.clear();
        }
        return;
    }
    for (id, buf) in &lines.0 {
        let off = id.world_offset();
        let off = Vec3::new(off[0], off[1], off[2]);
        for l in buf {
            gizmos.line(
                Vec3::from(l.a) + off,
                Vec3::from(l.b) + off,
                // rapier's DebugRenderStyle emits HSLA, not RGBA.
                Color::hsla(l.color[0], l.color[1], l.color[2], l.color[3]),
            );
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// F3 toggles the debug overlay's visibility — and with it the collider
/// wireframe view (one debug mode): the shared flag tells the game thread
/// whether to generate lines at all.
pub fn toggle_debug(
    keys: Res<ButtonInput<KeyCode>>,
    flags: Res<super::collider_debug::DebugFlagsRes>,
    mut overlay: Query<&mut Visibility, With<DebugOverlay>>,
) {
    if !keys.just_pressed(KeyCode::F3) {
        return;
    }
    for mut vis in &mut overlay {
        *vis = match *vis {
            Visibility::Hidden => Visibility::Visible,
            _ => Visibility::Hidden,
        };
        flags.0.set_collider_wireframes(*vis == Visibility::Visible);
    }
}
```
